learn.hook: Look closely! A picture is full of tiny stories.
points: First look at the whole picture. Then look at each part.
Say what you see: "I can see a cat."
Tell the colour and size: "I can see a big red ball."
Tell how many: "I can see two birds."
Tell where: "The cat is under the tree."

example.q: Look: 🌳🐒🐒🐒 (three monkeys near a tree). Tell about the picture in one sentence.
steps: What do I see? Monkeys and a tree.
How many monkeys? Count: 1, 2, 3.
Put it together in a sentence.
example.answer: I can see three monkeys near a tree.

learn.reallife: When Dadu shows us old photos, we tell him who we see and what they are doing.

games.title: Picture talk: true or false?
items: "I can see a cat" tells what is in a picture.
It names the thing we see.
An elephant is smaller than an ant.
An elephant is big. An ant is small.
Big and small tell about size.
They tell how large a thing is.
🌞 is a picture of the moon.

quiz.q: Look: 🐄🐄. How many cows can you see?
quiz.explain: Count the cows: 1, 2. There are two cows.
steps: Count the cows: 1, 2.
There are 2 cows.

quiz.q: Look: 🐦🐦🐦🐦 on a wire. How many birds?
steps: Count the birds: 1, 2, 3, 4.
There are 4 birds.

quiz.q: Look: 🐘 and 🐭. Which one is big?
quiz.explain: An elephant is big. A mouse is small.
steps: An elephant is very big. A mouse is very small.
So the elephant is big.

quiz.q: Which sentence tells about 🌳🐱 (a cat under a tree)?
options: The cat is on the moon.
The cat is under the tree.
The tree is in the cat.
quiz.explain: The cat sits under the tree, so we say "under the tree".
steps: Look at the picture. The cat is below the tree.
So we say, 'The cat is under the tree.'
quiz.mistake: Does not match the words to the picture

quiz.q: Look: 🎈 (a red balloon). Which word tells its colour?
steps: Red tells us the colour.
Round tells the shape. Balloon is the name.
Answer: Red
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape word or naming word for colour

quiz.q: What is a good way to start telling about a picture?
quiz.explain: "I can see" tells what is in the picture.
steps: We tell what is in the picture.
So we begin with 'I can see ...'
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to begin describing

teach.ask: Gappu: My Nani sent me a picture. How do I tell about it?
teach.praise: I can see a happy Gappu! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Can I tell the colour, size or how many?

revise.summary: To tell about a picture, look at the whole picture first, then say what you see, its colour and size, how many and where it is.
focus: Make a sentence that begins 'I can see ...'
remember: Tell colour and size: I can see a big red ball.
Tell where: The cat is under the tree.
traps: Don't skip or count twice when you count.
Don't mix up a colour word (red) with a shape word (round).

learn.hook: Everything has a name. Even your toothbrush!
points: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing.
Cat, cow, parrot and tiger are names of animals.
Bag, cup, ball and chair are names of things.
We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds: an apple, an egg, an owl.
We use a before other sounds: a cat, a bag, a dog.

example.q: Think it through: Is it "a egg" or "an egg"?
steps: Say egg. It begins with the e sound.
a, e, i, o, u are vowels.
We use an before a vowel sound.

learn.reallife: In the kitchen we can name many things: a cup, a plate, a spoon and an onion!

quiz.q: Which is the name of an animal?
quiz.explain: A tiger is an animal. A table and a pencil are things.
steps: A tiger is an animal.
A table and a pencil are things.
Answer: Tiger

quiz.q: Which is the name of a thing?
quiz.explain: We eat with a spoon. It is a thing, not an animal.
steps: A spoon is a thing. We eat with it.
A goat and a peacock are animals.
Answer: Spoon

quiz.q: 🍎 Choose the right words for this picture.
quiz.explain: Apple begins with the a sound, a vowel. So we say an apple.
steps: Say apple. It begins with the a sound.
A, e, i, o, u are vowels. We use an before a vowel sound.
One apple, so: an apple.
quiz.mistake: Uses a before a vowel sound

quiz.q: 🐕 Which words name this pet the right way?
quiz.explain: Dog begins with d, not a vowel. So we say a dog.
steps: Say dog. It begins with d. D is not a vowel.
We use a before other sounds. One dog, so: a dog.

quiz.q: Read: "The parrot sits on a branch." Which word names a bird?
quiz.explain: Parrot is the name of a bird.
steps: A parrot is a bird.
Sits is an action word. So parrot names the bird.
quiz.mistake: Picks an action word instead of a naming word

quiz.q: ⚽ Which is the right spelling for this toy?
steps: Say the sounds: b-a-l-l.
Ball has two l letters at the end: ball.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out a letter or uses the wrong vowel

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a naming word? And when do I say an?
teach.praise: An excellent answer! I mean, a great answer!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me some names of animals or things?

revise.summary: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing. We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds and a before other sounds.
focus: Sort names into animals and things
Choose a or an before a word
remember: an apple, an egg, an owl (a, e, i, o, u sounds)
a cat, a bag, a dog (other sounds)
Animals: cat, cow, parrot, tiger. Things: bag, cup, ball, chair.
traps: Don't say 'a apple'. Say an apple.
Don't use an before every word. It is a dog.
